nodes.name: High-temperature flux synthesis
nodes.procedure: Reagent grade nickel(II) oxide (NiO, Wako Pure Chemical Industries), iron(III) oxide (Fe_2O_3, Wako Pure Chemical Industries), and sodium nitrate (NaNO_3, Wako Pure Chemical Industries) were used as nickel, iron, and flux precursors, respectively. The solute concentration was fixed at 40 mol% for NaNO_3 flux. NiO and Fe_2O_3 were isolated via ball milling at 500 rpm for 2 h by using ethanol as the dispersion reagent. The NiO, Fe_2O_3, and NaNO_3 powders were placed in a mortar and ground for 15 min. The obtained homogeneous powder was introduced in an aluminum crucible (30 cm^3), loosely covered by a lid, and placed in a muffle furnace. Subsequently, it was heated in four steps: (i) The temperature was increased at a rate of 500°C h^{-1} until a temperature of 700°C was reached. (ii) The temperature was increased from 700 to 800°C at a rate of 60°C h^{-1}. (iii) The temperature was maintained at 800°C for 10 h. (iv) The temperature was decreased to 300°C at a rate of 200°C h^{-1}. The obtained NiFe LDH oxide precursor (NaNi_{0.75}Fe_{0.25}O_2) was denoted as NiFe LDH-Pre.

nodes.description: Batch adsorption capacity testing for phosphate ions
nodes.source_text: The adsorption capacities of NiFe LDH-Top@Cl for phosphate, fluoride, and nitrate ions were 194.92, 176.15, and 146.28 mg g^{-1} respectively. The adsorption capacity toward all the anions reached over 70% within 10 min.

nodes.description: Batch adsorption capacity testing for fluoride ions
nodes.source_text: The adsorption capacities of NiFe LDH-Top@Cl for phosphate, fluoride, and nitrate ions were 194.92, 176.15, and 146.28 mg g^{-1} respectively. The adsorption capacity toward all the anions reached over 70% within 10 min.

nodes.description: Batch adsorption capacity testing for nitrate ions
nodes.source_text: The adsorption capacities of NiFe LDH-Top@Cl for phosphate, fluoride, and nitrate ions were 194.92, 176.15, and 146.28 mg g^{-1} respectively. The adsorption capacity toward all the anions reached over 70% within 10 min.

The values of the saturated adsorption capacity for all anions calculated by using the pseudo-second-order model (q_t2) were closer than those calculated by using the pseudo-first-order model (q_t1)... These findings showed that the anions adsorbed on NiFe LDH-Top@Cl followed the pseudo-second-order kinetics assumption, indicating that the rate-determining step was controlled by the chemisorption mechanism.

The correlation coefficient for the Langmuir model (R_L²) was higher than that of the Freundlich and D-R model. Hence, the adsorption process followed the Langmuir model... The E values of phosphate... were found to be approximately 21.29–23.26 kJ mol^{-1}, indicating that the adsorption was controlled by chemical adsorption.

The ΔH⁰ values of all the anions were negative, suggesting that the adsorption was exothermic. The ΔS° values were positive... Furthermore, the negative ΔG° values were attributed to their spontaneous nature.

after the five tests, the adsorption capacity of NiFe LDH-Top@Cl for phosphate, fluoride, and nitrate ions decreased by 6.84%, 8.46%, and 7.18%, respectively... NiFe LDH-Top@Cl maintained a removal efficiency of over 90% for all the anions after the five tests, indicating high stability.
NiFe LDH-Pre exhibited poor adsorption capacity toward all anions. This might be due to the lack of electronic charges on its structure.
The adsorption capacity of NiFe LDH-Top was significantly lower than that of NiFe LDH-Top@Cl. This was because the bonding of CO_3^{2-} ions in the interlayer was stronger than that of Cl^- ions

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-Top and NiFe LDH-Top@Cl show diffraction patterns corresponding to 003, 006, 012, 015, 018, 110, and 113 planes of brucite-like hydroxides with 003 plane at 2θ = 12.98° and 11.46° respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe LDH-Top and NiFe LDH-Top@Cl showed similar diffraction pattern corresponding to the 003, 006, 012, 015, 018, 110, and 113 planes, which were the typical indications of brucite-like hydroxides (ICDD PDF 330429).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-Pre shows peaks at 1423 and 744 cm⁻¹ for N-O stretching and M-O-M vibrations; NiFe LDH-Top and NiFe LDH-Top@Cl show O-H stretching at 3400 cm⁻¹, O-H bending at 1637 cm⁻¹, and C-O stretching of CO₃²⁻ at 1344 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe LDH-Pre exhibited peaks at 1423 and 744 cm⁻¹ which were attributed to the N-O stretching and M-O-M lattice mode vibrations, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-Pre shows Ni 2p3/2 at 855.0 eV and Ni 2p1/2 at 876.7 eV (Ni3+); NiFe LDH-Top and NiFe LDH-Top@Cl show Ni 2p3/2 at 856.3 eV and Ni 2p1/2 at 874.0 eV (Ni2+), Fe 2p3/2 at 712.7 eV and Fe 2p1/2 at 725.9 eV (Fe3+).
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe LDH-Pre showed a valence state of 3+ at 855.0 and 876.7 eV and the satellite state at 862.2 and 879.9 eV. Conversely, ... replaced by a valence state of 2+ at 856.3 and 874.0 eV ... Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 peaks ... ascribed to the binding of a valence state of 3+ (712.7 and 725.9 eV).

nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental dispersion mapping of NiFe LDHs-Top@Cl is illustrated in Figure 5b. Ni, Fe, O, and Cl were homogeneously distributed throughout the particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-Pre shows type III isotherm (nonporous); NiFe LDH-Top and NiFe LDH-Top@Cl show type IV with H3 hysteresis indicating slit-like mesopores. BET surface areas: 35.24, 159.26, 163.13 m²g⁻¹ respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe LDH-Pre demonstrated the type III isotherm, indicating the characteristic of a nonporous material ... The specific surface areas of NiFe LDH-Pre, NiFe LDH-Top, NiFe LDH-Top@Cl ... were 35.24, 159.26, 163.13 ... m²g⁻¹, respectively.
